game.name: Cult of the Lamb
game.short_description: Start your own cult in a land of false prophets, venturing out into diverse and mysterious regions to build a loyal community of woodland Followers and spread your Word to become the one true cult.

other_scores.score: Very Positive, about 93% (469 reviews at launch)

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Cult of the Lamb is a management sim fused with an action roguelite: you tend a cult village between short dungeon runs. He feels combining two very different design approaches leaves both halves underdeveloped, with minimal building and underwhelming combat. He nonetheless got invested thanks to the art and characters and recommends it, placing it just above Children of Morta rather than naming a letter tier.
praise: Art style and visuals are superb and drew him into the cult and its characters
Looking forward to returning to the village to check on followers
Finding new map locations felt rewarding and built the world
Ambitious attempt to merge two genres is respected
criticism: Runs are super short (around three rooms), so strong build combinations rarely matter
Low replay value once the village is built and the game finished
unique_points: Combines a village management sim with an action roguelite, splitting time between the two
Short runs are dictated by the need to tend the village, which some players like
commentary.quote: gameplay wise not a huge fan but I did really enjoy playing it
design_criteria: Genre blending: two design approaches each left not fully fleshed out
Run length: very short runs undermine build power
Replayability: drops after the first completion

community.one_liner: A cute-but-macabre action roguelite from Massive Monster (published by Devolver Digital, 2022) where you play a sacrificed lamb who founds a cult, alternating between dungeon runs and managing a village of followers.
community.consensus_summary: Cult of the Lamb is received as a highly successful, charming genre blend: critics sit at Metacritic 82 (88 reviews) and OpenCritic 84 (143 reviews, 88% recommend), and Steam players rate it Overwhelmingly Positive (about 96% of 130k reviews). Praise centres on art, music, tone and the addictive loop between combat and cult management; criticism centres on thin combat depth, limited run variety and management that can turn into micromanagement. It has been supported for years with free updates and paid DLC (Sinful Pack, Pilgrim Pack, and the large Woolhaven expansion in January 2026), and is not early access or abandoned. A minority of players find both halves shallow or repetitive, and Woolhaven launch brought some save-corruption and bug complaints.
best_things: Distinctive cute-meets-dark art style, humour and tone; very widely praised
Catchy, memorable soundtrack that players mention repeatedly
Combat is responsive, fast and easy to pick up, with short, satisfying dungeon runs
The loop of running dungeons to feed cult management, then returning to build, is called addictive and cozy
Emotional attachment to followers (naming, marrying, reviving them, grieving deaths) creates stories players love
Strong accessibility and difficulty options let players with disabilities or different skill levels enjoy it
Generous free post-launch content and later DLC; co-op on the Steam version
Rich lore, hidden quests and steady new unlocks keep progression engaging for fans (though some find the ending and final boss underwhelming)
worst_things: Combat is shallow compared with Hades or Binding of Isaac: few real builds, limited weapon/curse variety and little run-to-run difference
Dungeons start to feel samey once you have cleared several; repetition sets in over time
The two halves do not fully integrate and some critics call it two genres each done competently but not deeply
Vague or unexplained mechanics and building descriptions, which the game then punishes you for missing
Bugs and technical issues: performance on some platforms, menu pause not stopping the village simulation, and save corruption reports around DLC
Enemy bullets and clutter can be hard to read, and healing items are rare, so early damage can ruin a run
Endgame does not go as far as other roguelites for players wanting huge replayability
improvements: Add more combat depth: parry mechanics, more build-defining weapon and curse synergies and more run variety
Explain systems, quests and building effects better in-game
Split-screen or independent village play in co-op so the second player is not tethered and idle during management
Fix save corruption and pause behavior; clearer timers that do not punish absences
More variety between dungeon layouts and more endgame replay incentives
Clearer readability of enemies and projectiles
unique_things: Fuses an action roguelite with a cult-running colony sim (Animal Crossing/Stardew style) in one loop
Adorable woodland-animal aesthetic used to tell a dark, sacrificial cult story with black humour
Followers have traits, loyalty and lives; you can indoctrinate, marry, sacrifice or revive them
Choose moral direction of your cult through doctrines, rituals and sermons, with real tradeoffs
Side activities like fishing, farming, gambling and decorating plus a large cosmetic/customisation set
Woolhaven adds winter, animal husbandry and new enemies as a second campaign-scale layer
tedious_or_disliked: Constant follower needs (feeding, cleaning waste, curing illness, sermons, quests) can feel like chores or laundry rather than fun
Day/night pressure and timed follower quests add stress and a sense of maintenance over achievement
Unlock pace slows sharply after the first ~6 hours, with long unlock animations and grindy costs, so progress feels slower over time
Losing part of your haul on death and rare healing feels punishing to players who came for base building
Grinding resources and travelling between activities (for example fishing just to support base management) feels like busywork to some
In co-op, the village management phase leaves one player bored or left out
Followers age and die quickly, and naming or bonding with them makes deaths and forced sacrifices feel bad for some players
divisive_points: Difficulty and roguelike elements: developers said they are core, while some players want them softened; others find Normal just right and praise the difficulty options
Whether the management half is relaxing and cozy or stressful micromanagement
Whether the game-of-two-halves structure is a strength or means neither half is excellent
Whether the game is a masterpiece or merely a charming, repetitive game carried by style
community.reception_notes: Launched Aug 11 2022 on PC, consoles and later iOS to strong critic scores and big sales (Steam Revenue Calculator estimates roughly $116M gross, about $34M net to the developer; SteamSpy owners 2-5M; estimates only, not audited). Steam price $24.99 and it is often discounted. The game kept receiving free updates and paid content; Woolhaven (Jan 22 2026) reportedly sold over 60,000 copies on Steam at launch and outsold earlier add-ons, though some players reported save corruption and bugs, especially when adding or removing DLC. Steam and OpenCritic user scores are high, while Metacritic user score (7.9, 70% positive) is notably lower than Steam, suggesting more mixed sentiment there. Available on Windows and macOS on Steam, not Linux.
